messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Sudden QPS spike detected for org=aperture-labs — sustained 6x above baseline for 3m, error rate rising from 0.2% to 1.8%. Autoscale healthy but per-org RL hitting limits.
oncall-alex: Got the page, joining. Any customer-facing impact reported?
cs-luis: Customer CS said timeouts on inference requests for a small cohort. Some requests got 429s. They flagged urgent.
sre-jen: Looking at org-level throttles — Aperture-Labs is on standard tier (200 QPS burst). Their traffic pattern is sudden ramp from a batch job. We can either raise their quota temporarily or soft-throttle noisy hosts.
eng-tom: If we bump per-org limit, risk extra load on pool. Alternative: disable semantic-rerank feature for that org (it's heavy) — that will drop cost per request by ~30%. Can we feature-flag it off?
oncall-alex: Can you toggle it quickly? What's the impact on quality?
eng-tom: Quality dip expected but CS said degradation tolerable short-term. Toggle command: ``/ff toggle aperture-labs semantic-rerank OFF --reason "emergency qps relief"`` — I can run if SRE approves.
sre-jen: Prefer per-org emergency RL patch first: increase org_limit from 200 -> 400 QPS for 30m, then monitor. If pool QPS stays high we'll hit overall capacity alarms. I'll apply transient override and watch.
eng-tom: Ok applying feature-flag fallback as a backup. If SRE applies RL patch and we still see high errors then flip FF.
cs-luis: Notifying customer that we're applying a temporary quota increase and may toggle rerank. Will send a short note now.
pm-anya: Track rollout decision in incident channel and capture timeline for postmortem. Also capture burst source (scheduled job?).
sre-jen: Applying emergency org RL override now: ``POST /api/internal/orgs/aperture-labs/override {"qps":400, "ttl_minutes":30, "reason":"emergency spike"}`` — done. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: ACTION: org_qps_override applied for aperture-labs by sre-jen at 2026-03-17T12:05:10Z, new limit=400 QPS, ttl=30m.
sre-jen: Metrics show 429s dropping within 60s, latency improving. Keep an eye on aggregate GPU queues.
eng-tom: Flipped semantic-rerank FF OFF for aperture-labs as precaution. Command: ``/ff toggle aperture-labs semantic-rerank OFF`` — done.
oncall-alex: Thanks. CS, confirm customer note sent?
cs-luis: Sent: "We see a traffic surge; we've temporarily increased your throughput and disabled rerank to stabilize requests. We will follow up with timeline and root cause." They replied OK.
pm-anya: Good. Assigning action items: SRE to monitor and extend or rollback override; Eng to investigate job pattern; CS to keep customer posted; PM to schedule postmortem.
sre-jen: Monitoring for 15m window. If cluster load >85% I'll throttle back the override and coordinate capacity.
incident-bot: ALERT: cluster_gpu_util at 72% (stable). 429s down to 0.3%.
oncall-alex: Handing off to SRE for watch. I'll go offline in 10. If anything changes, page me.
sre-jen: Acknowledged. Will escalate if regressions.
eng-tom: Noted — collecting request traces and origin IPs, will post a short summary.
cs-luis: Customer appreciated the quick action. They want a follow-up tomorrow.
pm-anya: Closing note here once metrics stable and override TTL near expiry.
incident-bot: INFO: override TTL expires in 10m.
sre-jen: Extending override +30m as traffic still elevated but stable: ``PATCH /api/internal/overrides/aperture-labs {"extend_minutes":30}" — done. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: ACTION: override extended to total ttl=60m by sre-jen.
oncall-alex: Thanks team. I'll file the incident and link to this thread. Postmortem owner assigned: pm-anya.
pm-anya: I'll own the postmortem. Quick summary I'll use: temporary QPS surge from scheduled batch; emergency org-level QPS override + feature flag rollback reduced 429s; follow-ups: investigate job cadence, consider auto-burst protection, add alert for sudden org ramp.
sre-jen: Marking incident resolved for now — will close after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: RESOLVED: incident state set to monitoring.
